name: m̀sə̀r, the « kotoko » speech of Kousseri
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress; 1 further work by the same author (or citing it for stress) agrees.
catalog_citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2019. Le syntagme nominal dans le parler « kotoko » de Kousseri. In Henry Tourneux & Yvonne Treis (eds), Topics in Chadic Linguistics X: Papers from the 9th Biennial International Colloquium on the Chadic Languages (Villejuif, September 7-8, 2017), in memoriam Russell Schuh, 241-257. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. HAL open preprint halshs-03226997.
catalog_locator: Section « Phonologie », HAL preprint p. 5 (header page number of 17), the whole section (two paragraphs);present. page in the Köppe volume not verifiable from the preprint (c. p. 244-245).
catalog_quote: Le m̀sə̀r compte 33 consonnes auxquelles s’ajoute une nasale syllabique attestée uniquement à l’initiale. Parmi ces consonnes, on relève un ordre fourni de labiovélaires – kw, gw, ŋw, hw, ɣw – ainsi qu’une série de deux éjectives – s’, ƙ. Contrairement au parler voisin de Logone-Birni, le m̀sə̀r n’a pas de latérales fricatives. Le système vocalique présente phonétiquement 6 voyelles brèves (i, e, a, o, u ə), qu’il n’est pas très difficile de réduire à 2 (a, ə) structurellement. Le système tonal compte deux registres (Haut et Bas) comme toutes les autres langues « kotoko ». Des tons modulés peuvent occasionnellement se rencontrer, sur des emprunts, par exemple.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: Mser has 33 consonants, to which is added a syllabic nasal attested only word-initially. [...] The vowel system phonetically shows 6 short vowels (i, e, a, o, u, ə), which it is not very hard to reduce to 2 (a, ə) structurally. The tone system has two registers (High and Low), like all the other 'Kotoko' languages. Contour tones can occasionally be met, on loanwords for example.
new_statements.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2019. Le syntagme nominal dans le parler « kotoko » de Kousseri. In H. Tourneux & Y. Treis (eds), Topics in Chadic Linguistics X (BICCL 9, Villejuif 2017), 241-257. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. HAL halshs-03226997.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (HAL halshs-03226997, 17 PDF pages, text present; the PDF's metadata gives the Title 'Le syntagme nominal dans le parler kotoko de Kousseri', Author Henry Tourneux, Creator HAL). extracted text of PDF page 6 (header page number 5) gives, under the heading 'Phonologie', exactly the quoted text: 'Le m̀sə̀r compte 33 consonnes auxquelles s'ajoute une nasale syllabique attestée uniquement à l'initiale. [..] Le système vocalique présente phonétiquement 6 voyelles brèves (i, e, a, o, u ə), qu'il n'est pas très difficile de réduire à 2 (a, ə) structurellement. Le système tonal compte deux registres (Haut et Bas) comme toutes les autres langues « kotoko ». Des tons modulés peuvent occasionne…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mser is described as a two-register (H/L) tone language, like the rest of Kotoko; the only published description of the language says nothing about word stress or accent at all. Tone is lexically and grammatically active (feminine derivation bə̀skwàn 'horse' / bə̀skwán 'mare'; tone-pattern change is one of the plural-formation devices; the relative marker rí raises the tone of the following noun, preprint p. 8). No stress placement rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: Contour (modulated) tones occur occasionally, e.g. on loanwords; otherwise only level H and L.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the lexical tone system of the word (nouns in citation and in noun-phrase context); the paper is a noun-phrase study with a one-page phonological sketch, transcriptions are largely surface-phonetic (note 1). Word stress is not discussed in any domain.
new_statements.identity_note: Tourneux 2019 describes the « kotoko » speech of the town of Kousseri, autonym [m̀sə̀r], which is exactly Glottolog's Mser (mser1242, ISO kqx; alt. names Kuseri/Kousseri/Msir/Klesem). Tourneux places it with Lagwan, Houlouf and Kala-Kafra in 'Kotoko central' (Gravina 2014: Kotoko Centre = Lagwan + Mser). Data are from Kousseri-town speakers recorded in 2000 (informants born 1928-1960); Ethnologue's other dialect names (Gawi, Houlouf, Kabe, Kalo) are not covered. The language is moribund (Campbell et al. 2022 via Glottolog).

new_statements.quote: 3. Il n'existe pas de consonne prénasalisée en KOTOKO. En synchronie, la consonne nasale dans le groupe NC- à l'initiale est syllabique quand le ton qu'elle porte est différent de celui de la syllabe qui suit. Elle est non syllabique généralement lorsque la syllabe qui la suit est homotone. La nasale N dans NC- est le vestige d'une syllabe disparue. [...] 12. Il ya une fréquente inversion du schème tonal entre afadé et maltam.
new_statements.translation: 3. There is no prenasalized consonant in KOTOKO. Synchronically, the nasal consonant in a word-initial NC- cluster is syllabic when the tone it bears is different from that of the following syllable. It is generally non-syllabic when the following syllable has the same tone. The nasal N in NC- is the vestige of a lost syllable. [...] 12. There is a frequent inversion of the tonal scheme between Afadé and Maltam.
new_statements.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2003. Le système consonantique des langues dites « kotoko ». In H. E. Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics (BICCL 1, Leipzig 2001), 115-135. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. HAL halshs-00349309 (open file, but behind HAL's Anubis anti-bot gate; no archived copy at the Internet Archive).

Remarques' with remark 3 exactly as quoted: 'Il n’existe pas de consonne prénasalisée en KOTOKO. En synchronie, la consonne nasale dans le groupe NC- à l’initiale est syllabique quand le ton qu’elle porte est différent de celui de la syllabe qui suit. Elle est non syllabique généralement lorsque la syllabe qui la suit est homotone. La nasale N dans NC- est le vestige d’une syllabe disparue.' p. 20 (footer 19) has remark 12 verbatim, including the source's own typo 'Il ya': '12. Il ya une fréquente…
new_statements.relation_note: Agrees with the existing statement (Tourneux 2019: two-register tone system, no mention of stress) at the level of type: the language group is presented as tonal and nothing is said about stress. The tone remark is made for KOTOKO as a group (excluding Buduma), not for Kousseri specifically, so it adds no Kousseri-specific detail.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The paper treats the 'kotoko' languages (sub-groups 2-4, Kousseri /msr/ among them) as tonal: every form is marked for low/high (and occasionally falling) tone, and the syllabicity of a word-initial nasal is stated to depend on whether its tone differs from that of the next syllable. There is no statement anywhere about word stress, accent or prominence, for Kousseri or any other variety.
new_statements.exceptions: none (no stress statement); remark 12 notes tonal-scheme inversion between Afadé and Maltam, which are other varieties
new_statements.identity_note: Both works are comparative across the 'kotoko' cluster; the Kousseri variety (= mser1242) appears as 'Kou / msŒr (Kousseri)' in Tourneux 2006 (preprint p. 3) and as 'kousseri /msr/' in Tourneux 2003 (classification p. 1, inventory p. 2). The tone remark quoted from Tourneux 2003 (remark 3) is stated for KOTOKO as a whole (sub-groups septentrional, central, méridional; Buduma excluded), not for Kousseri alone; remark 12 concerns Afadé and Maltam, different varieties (Afade afa1241, Maltam malt1245-type varieties), not Kousseri.

sources.note: A Martinet-school (functionalist) morphosyntax thesis on predicate, aspect and utterance types in Kousseri Kotoko; such theses normally open with a phonological inventory including the tones used in transcription, and any account of aspect marking in a Kotoko language has to deal with tonal morphology (cf. Tourneux 2007 on tonal inversion), so a two-tone (H/L) statement and tone-marked data are likely but unverified. It would be the only monograph-length first-hand description of Mser.
